text:
Ava (People Ops): Thanks for the great questions during the all-hands. Moving follow-ups here so everyone's looped. Quick headline: calibration next Wed, comp letters ~June 18, retroactive effective dates possible for special cases.
Elena (CEO): Appreciate the energy. Our goal is consistency + transparency. We'll share more context behind high-level decisions after calibration.
Sophie L.: Can managers share concrete examples they used in calibration? Would help us understand where to focus next cycle.
Raj (VP Eng): Yes — managers should include 3-5 bullet accomplishments tied to metrics or product outcomes. We'll publish anonymous examples.
Marcus (CTO): For engineering examples, think: shipped cross-team feature that increased throughput by X%, reduced infra cost by Y, or owned rollout reducing error rate by Z.
Daren: If I'm promoted retroactively to May 1, do I get backpay?
Priya (Finance): Retroactive promos can get backpay to the effective date if approved before payroll close. We'll confirm based on the approval date.
Jules (Recruiting): Does promotion affect leveling for ICs vs managers differently? Curious about transition guidance.
Ava (People Ops): For IC -> manager transitions we'll provide a transition checklist (expectations, 1:1 cadence, probation checkpoints). Leveling impacts comp bands and title alignment.
Kim: Any update on spot bonuses or discretionary recognition this quarter?
Ava (People Ops): We have a small recognition fund for exceptional contributions. Managers can nominate through the form on docs/people-ops; approvals are fast-tracked during calibration window.
Sophie L.: Will there be a public list of who got promoted? We prefer private first then public announcement.
Elena (CEO): Promotions will be communicated privately to the individual first, then a celebratory announcement in #all-hands the following week unless the employee requests delay.
oncall-bot: Reminder: calibration window opens 2026-06-10.
Ava (People Ops): Here's the short timeline snippet I promised:
```
Week 1: Manager submissions due
Week 2: Calibration meetings
Week 3: Outcome notifications + comp letters
Week 4: Public announcements
```
Daren: What's the expected size of promotion increases? Ballpark % for L3->L4 and L4->L5?
Priya (Finance): Ballparks vary by role and market. Typical ranges: L3->L4: 7-12%, L4->L5: 10-18%. Equity refreshes handled separately. Exact numbers in offer/comp letters.
Marcus (CTO): For engineering, if someone's scope expanded but title didn't, raise that with your manager now so it's included in calibration.
Sophie L.: Is there a formal process to request more mentoring or cross-team opportunities to support promotion?
Raj (VP Eng): Yes — managers should create a development plan with specific projects/mentorship and flag it in the submission. We encourage stretch assignments.
Kim: Quick Q re: healthcare opt-ins for dependents mid-year? Any changes?
Ava (People Ops): Mid-year dependent enrollment is allowed for qualifying life events. Otherwise wait for open enrollment. Email benefits@redwood.com for cases.
Ava (People Ops): We'll compile these Qs + answers into a short FAQ and post in #docs/people-ops by Monday. If you need confidentiality, DM me or email people-ops@redwood.com. Leaving thread open for 72 hours for follow-ups. Thanks all!
